$comment: Advisories consciously accepted, with an expiry date that forces re-review.
This is NOT a way to silence the audit gate: scripts/audit-gate.mjs fails the
build for any advisory that is not listed here, and ALSO fails for any entry
whose reviewBy date has passed. Adding an entry requires a real applicability

allow.title: React Router: RSC Mode CSRF Bypass Allows Action Execution Before 400 Response
justification: NOT REACHABLE IN THIS APPLICATION. The advisory affects React Router's RSC
mode, where a server executes a route `action` before returning 400. DriveMy
is a purely client-side SPA: src/App.tsx uses the declarative <BrowserRouter>
with plain <Route element={...}>. It does not use createBrowserRouter,
RouterProvider, route `loader`/`action` data APIs, or any server runtime —
there is no server to execute an action on.
NO FORWARD FIX EXISTS. The advisory declares the vulnerable range as
>=7.12.0 <8.3.0, but react-router-dom 8.x has never been published (latest
on npm is 7.18.2 as of 2026-08-03). npm's suggested remediation is a
DOWNGRADE to 7.11.0, which it flags as semver-major and which would forfeit
seven minor releases of unrelated fixes.
ACTION ON EXPIRY: re-check whether react-router 8.3.0+ has shipped. If it
has, plan the major upgrade and delete this entry. If the app ever adopts
createBrowserRouter or any data-router API, delete this entry immediately —
the applicability argument above no longer holds.
